# Quick Start

**Read online (recommended):**

1. Open your browser and go to: `https://altustd.github.io/causal-inference-python-ebook/`
2. Use the sidebar to navigate between chapters.
3. Use the search icon (top right) to search the full text.

**Download PDF:**

On the online version, click the download icon (top right of any page) and select PDF.

**Run code locally:** See Section 4.

\newpage

# HTML Navigation

The HTML version is the primary format. Key features:

- **Sidebar:** Full table of contents with part and chapter navigation.
- **Search:** Click the magnifying glass icon or press `/` to search all text, equations, and code.
- **Code folding:** Click "Code" buttons to show or hide individual code blocks.
- **Dark mode:** Toggle in the top navigation bar.
- **Equation rendering:** All equations use MathJax; they render in any modern browser.

# Reproducing the Code

All Python code in the book is executable and reproducible.

## Install pixi

```bash
# macOS / Linux
curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | bash

# Windows (PowerShell)
iwr -useb https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Clone and Set Up

```bash
git clone https://github.com/altustd/causal-inference-python-ebook.git
cd causal-inference-python-ebook
pixi install
pixi run setup
```

## Render Locally

```bash
pixi run render       # HTML → docs/index.html
pixi run render-pdf   # PDF → docs/Uncertain-Minds.pdf
pixi run preview      # live preview at http://localhost:4321
```

# Glossary

**Bayesian inference:** The process of updating prior beliefs in light of new evidence, using Bayes' theorem.

**Causal inference:** The discipline concerned with identifying cause-and-effect relationships from data.

**Confounders:** Variables that influence both a treatment and an outcome, creating spurious associations.

**DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph):** A graph with directed edges and no cycles, used to encode causal structure.

**Do-calculus:** Pearl's formal language for reasoning about interventions.

**Fuzzy set:** A set whose members have graded (partial) membership rather than all-or-nothing membership.

**Membership function:** A function mapping each element to its degree of membership in a fuzzy set.

**MCMC:** Markov Chain Monte Carlo — a class of algorithms for sampling from probability distributions.

**Posterior:** The updated probability distribution after incorporating observed data.

**Prior:** The probability distribution over parameters before observing data.

**Prototype:** The most typical or central member of a category, around which the category is organized.

**Reinforcement learning:** A learning framework in which an agent learns a policy by maximizing cumulative reward through interaction with an environment.
